signals: No application or interaction layer exists
The user has defined a new standalone desktop workflow
evidence: User outcomes and data sources
State, persistence, supported-platform, and distribution boundaries

signals: Stable public APIs already implement the use cases
The GUI can run safely in the same process
evidence: Public entry points and ownership rules
Threading, cancellation, and domain-level tests

signals: The TUI is one frontend over a tested application core
The GUI must preserve the TUI entry point
evidence: The TUI-to-core boundary
Core progress, error, and cancellation contracts

signals: The executable is the only supported integration boundary
It exposes versioned structured input and output
evidence: Structured protocol and version contract
Exit, cancellation, progress, and error semantics

signals: A service is the authoritative state and operation boundary
Connectivity and authentication are user-visible states
evidence: API schema and compatibility policy
Authentication, retry, timeout, and offline behavior

signals: The host exposes a supported embedded frontend extension point
The GUI shares the host lifecycle
evidence: Host ABI or API and event-loop contract
Load, unload, ownership, and distribution rules

signals: Users open files, configure an operation, and inspect output
A reusable library owns parsing and transformation
evidence: Supported file types and validation errors
Long-running operation and result ownership rules

signals: Users keep several editable documents open and arrange peer work surfaces
Project hierarchy, contextual commands, and diagnostics support a dominant editor canvas
evidence: Document identity, dirty state, persistence, and split ownership
Hierarchy, command routing, diagnostics, and close behavior

signals: Users directly arrange selectable objects in a spatial scene
The selected object drives hierarchy state, contextual tools, and editable properties
evidence: Scene graph, selection, transform, undo, and persistence contracts
Property model, play-test, diagnostics, and teardown behavior

signals: A local service discovers nearby endpoints and negotiates transfers
Users choose content and a destination, then follow acceptance, progress, completion, or failure
evidence: Discovery lifetime, endpoint identity, trust, and acceptance protocol
Transfer progress, retry, cancellation, and partial-failure behavior

signals: A composed preview remains active while sources and levels change
Operators must distinguish configured, armed, active, muted, failing, and stopped states immediately
evidence: Preview/output lifecycle, source ordering, and real-time update contracts
Metering, state transitions, start-stop safety, and recovery behavior

signals: A service owns a hierarchy of durable documents and structured records
Users edit one object through text, grid, board, or other peer representations
evidence: Workspace hierarchy, document identity, view schema, and persistence
Conflict, offline, synchronization, permission, and revision behavior

signals: A remote agent edits durable workspace artifacts from user prompts
Run diagnostics are useful but do not need a permanent inspector
evidence: Artifact lifecycle, revisions, and supported edit operations
Agent run, cancellation, and temporary diagnostic contracts

signals: A structured process reports ordered build stages and progress
Users retry failed stages and inspect step output
evidence: Stage identifiers, ordering, progress, and retry semantics
Structured output, cancellation, and failure contracts

signals: A library exposes a hierarchy of revisioned artifacts
Users compare, annotate, and approve precise locations
evidence: Artifact hierarchy, revision identity, and annotation model
Comparison, approval, persistence, and ownership APIs

signals: Session state is reconstructed from a sequenced event stream
Users inspect decisions, recovery boundaries, and replay position
evidence: Event sequence, snapshot, gap recovery, and replay contracts
Decision requests, completion, and connection state

signals: Several named agents own concurrent tasks and handoffs
Users monitor coordination, exceptions, and worker status
evidence: Agent identity, task ownership, and handoff state
Concurrency, failure, cancellation, and coordination APIs

retrieval_cases.intent: long growing event history with virtualized rows
